slides.title: Before you watch
slides.prompt: Imagine the hidden machinery running behind your social media feed.
slides.content:
• The Scale — How many fake accounts do you think exist online right now?
• The Disguise — What might a fake online account look like to fool you?
• Your Feed — Have you ever suspected a comment or account felt strangely inhuman?

A small automated robot
A program used only for advertising
A fake phone connected to the internet

Because platforms trust real devices and block suspicious ones

options.text: To make people interact with bots
To increase the number of fake accounts navigating the internet
To make posts look more entertaining
To influence what the algorithm shows people

options.text: To make them harder to be detected
To prevent them from using the same phones
To make their posts more creative and reliable
To reduce the cost of running the bot farm

options.text: The difficulty of controlling a bot farm
The conflict between real and fake users
The small mistakes and costs involved in real human activity
The time needed to create a social media account

questions.correctAnswer: The small mistakes and costs involved in real human activity

options.text: To make the video more entertaining
To show evidence of human effort and imperfection
To demonstrate how quickly bots can copy images
To explain how artificial intelligence generates pictures

questions.correctAnswer: To show evidence of human effort and imperfection

slides.title: Language focus: Future with 'going to'
slides.content:
The speaker uses 'going to' throughout this scene to signal intentions and predictions that feel inevitable or already planned. It sits between a simple promise and a certain future fact, which is exactly what makes it powerful in persuasive speech.
• Form: subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb (e.g. 'I am going to draw').
• Meaning: use it for plans already decided before the moment of speaking, or for predictions based on visible evidence.
• Use: in spoken persuasion, 'going to' creates urgency — it tells the listener something is already in motion and cannot be stopped.
In this scene 'going to' is the speaker's secret weapon: every time he says it, he makes the threat of bot farms feel not hypothetical but already happening.

words.translation: a pre-decided plan being announced to the listener right now
words.example: And I'm going to draw the whole thing by hand badly for one reason.

words.translation: a prediction based on clear evidence visible to the speaker
words.example: By the end, that reason is going to matter more than anything else, I tell you.

She is going to explains the algorithm to the class.
